newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast daily power slides on milder temps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast daily power slides on milder temps.

text.p: Bulk electricity prices for weekday delivery in the northeastern U.S. slid Friday on an outlook for temperatures in the region moderating from the current cold snap over weekend.
Thursday day-ahead prices in the Northeast jumped on the expected arrival of a brief cold spell through Saturday.

Outlook of milder weather also pressured natural gas prices. Swing natgas prices at the New York City gate dipped to the $4.90-$5.00 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) range from Thursday's $5.05 area.
Regional power prices fell despite an unplanned overnight outage of 1,137 megawatt (MW) of the Nine Mile Point 2 nuclear power plant.
The operator Niagara Mohawk Power Corp shut the Scriba, N.Y., unit late Thursday and began inspecting the steel beams around the reactor.
Niagara Mohawk officials could not immediately be reached for comment, but market sources said Nine Mile Point 2 could begin startup as early as Saturday.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) fell to $24.00-$25.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), down sharply from Thursday's $30.00-$35.00 for day-ahead power.
Off-peak, non-firm deliveries for Monday in western NYPP were pegged notationally lower at $15.00-$16.00 from Thursday's $16.00-$17.00.
In eastern NYPP, Monday's peak, non-firm power was valued at $28.00-$30.00/MWh. down from Thursday's $33.00-$39.00 for Friday.
Eastern NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Monday was steady from Thursday at $19.00-$20.00.
The 832 MW James A Fitzpatrick nuclear plant, also in Scriba, N.Y., reached 50 percent power after being shutting last Sunday to repair a leak in the electrical hydraulic control system.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Monday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border were quoted near $35.00/MWh, the lower end of Thursday's $35.00-$37.00 range.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Monday delivery to the NU border was down to $21.00-$22.00, down from $22.00-$23.00 Thursday.

The 910 MW Maine Yankee nuclear power plant could remain shut well into January as the operator and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission have started a three-week review of the plant's electrical cable system.
The plant was shut December 6 after engineers found a couple of cables to the plant's main control room had been improperly routed.
Today Maine Yankee's president Charles Frizzle resigned as the board of director seeks new leadership that could deal with "cultural issues" raised in a recent regulatory review.
